questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook sausages at a barbecue
Why vegetarians live longer than meat eaters
Whether plant-based meat substitutes are healthier than meat
The history of British sausages
questions.why: They find out whether plant-based foods really are a healthier alternative to meat.

questions.q: What does Georgie think of plant-based sausages and burgers?
options: She has never tried them
She likes them as long as they have plenty of sauce
She prefers them to real meat and eats them almost every day
She thinks they taste terrible
questions.why: Georgie says she quite likes them 'as long as they're covered in sauce'.

questions.q: What is Neil's opinion of plant-based meat alternatives?
options: They are much better than real meat and he now eats them every week
They are too expensive to buy
He refuses to eat them
They're fine, but maybe not as good as the real thing
questions.why: Neil says they're fine but he's 'not sure they're as good as the real thing'.

questions.q: What worries listener Graham Glover about vegetable sausages?
options: They are highly processed with lots of added ingredients
They contain hidden meat
They have too little protein
They are worse for the environment than pork sausages are
questions.why: He asks about how they're processed, 'full of additives and flavourings and colourings'.

questions.q: What is the protein in Quorn products made from?
options: A type of fungus
Soy beans and nuts
Milk and yoghurt
Wheat from bread
questions.why: Neil says Quorn uses mycoprotein, a fungi-based protein.

questions.q: How does Graham react when he hears that Quorn comes from a fungus?
options: He is disgusted and won't eat it
He is surprised and wants to learn much more about how it is made
He thinks it must be unhealthy
He doesn't mind – he only cares whether it's healthy
questions.why: He says he has no problem with that; it's just another form of protein and what matters is health.

questions.q: Why does presenter Greg Foot mention his mum?
options: To show that she agrees with Graham
To show a different view – she doesn't want it to resemble meat
To explain that she makes her own vegetable sausages at home every week
To say she has started eating meat again
questions.why: His mum, a long-time veggie, says she doesn't want her alternative proteins to resemble meat.

questions.q: What does Graham need from a plant-based sausage?
options: It must be cheaper than a pork sausage from the supermarket
It must be made at home
It must taste, feel and look like a meat sausage
It must contain no fungus
questions.why: He says it needs to be similar 'in terms of flavour, texture, and appearance'.
